phase1AsBuilt.naming: Icon/ThumbUpOutlined (MUI) and Icon/ThumbDownOutlined (MUI). The "(MUI)" suffix follows the established convention for glyphs that come from @mui/icons-material rather than from Tebra source — the same suffix carried by Icon/Cancel (MUI), Icon/Close (MUI), Icon/NavigateBefore (MUI), Icon/RadioUnchecked (MUI) and Icon/SearchOutlined (MUI).
phase1AsBuilt.source: @mui/icons-material/ThumbUpOutlined.js and ThumbDownOutlined.js at 5.15.12, wrapping the MUI Material Symbols path. 24 viewBox, SCALE constraints, single path with three subpaths (outer outline, interior counter, cuff).
phase1AsBuilt.windingRule: Set explicitly to NONZERO — the SVG default the MUI path is authored against. Set deliberately because of the WarningFilled precedent, where an import lost fill-rule and the interior counter filled in solid.
phase1AsBuilt.variableBinding: Both bind their vector fill to color/primary/main — VariableID:74:3, #004852, scopes [FRAME_FILL, SHAPE_FILL, TEXT_FILL, STROKE_COLOR].
phase1AsBuilt.publishStep: Already done before this phase. Both report CURRENT.

openDefectCarriedForward._severity: medium — recorded in Phase 1, still unresolved, and Phase 2 has now placed the affected glyph into a proposal that will be reviewed.
openDefectCarriedForward.finding: The library built the OUTLINED family; production uses the ALT family, which is a visibly different glyph — one unified shape with no separate cuff.
openDefectCarriedForward.evidence: No file imports ThumbUpOutlined or ThumbDownOutlined. The three feedback surfaces that do this job import: ThumbUpAltOutlined / ThumbDownAltOutlined in facesheet-ui RecommendationsFeedback.tsx:102,113 and messages-ui SuggestReplyControls.tsx:396,408; ThumbUpAlt / ThumbUpOffAlt / ThumbDownAlt / ThumbDownOffAlt in clinical-system SummaryFeedback.tsx:1-4.
openDefectCarriedForward.consequence: If the library is meant to match what ships, these should be the Alt glyphs. The proposal now shows a thumb that no production surface renders.
openDefectCarriedForward.status: FOR DECISION. Not resolved here because it is a library question, not a proposal question, and changing it would mean rebuilding and republishing two published icons.

thumbs.what: The two existing text Buttons in each Card instance Actions region were SWAPPED (not deleted, not detached) to Icon button instances carrying ThumbUp and ThumbDown.
thumbs.whySwapAndNotAdd: A Card instance cannot host new children. Repurposing the two buttons that were already in the Actions region avoids that constraint entirely — no scaffolding was needed for the thumbs.
thumbs.component: Icon button 170:77, variant color=default, size=small, State=Default. 34x34 with the glyph at 18x18, which is MUI IconButton size small.
thumbs.colourChange: The old buttons were color=primary (teal). The thumbs are color=default, so the glyph renders #545454. This is most of why the band reads calmer.
thumbs.gotcha: swapComponent preserves the old instance width/height as a fixed override — the swapped nodes came through at 64x36 and 101x36. resize() does not clear it. Setting layoutSizingHorizontal and layoutSizingVertical to HUG collapses them to the component natural 34x34. Recorded because it will recur on any Button-to-Icon-button swap.

infoIcon.whyNotInfoFilled: Icon/InfoFilled 164:10 is the Alert severity glyph — registered as MuiAlert defaultProps.iconMapping.info — and its path is byte-identical to AttentionFilledIcon. Using it on a card would collide with alert severity semantics. Outlined also matches the outlined thumbs.
infoIcon.placement: Content zone, card-relative x=8 y=106, so the glyph sits at x=16 flush with the text column, directly beneath the synthesis statement. Same position on all three cards.
infoIcon.placementWasForcedByMeasurement: Two more obvious placements were tested by measuring rendered text and both fail on card 2. Inline after the synthesis statement: card 2 last line is 422px wide in a 427px box, leaving 5px. Trailing the title: card 2 title is 412px wide in the same box, leaving 15px. Neither fits a 34px control. The measurement was done by greedy-wrapping each body string through a temporary text node at the real font and size, then removing it.
infoIcon.separationFromThumbs: Info is bottom-LEFT in the content zone at y=106. Thumbs are bottom-RIGHT in the action zone at y=128. Different row and different column, ~370px apart on a 459px card. The brief warned that three icons in a row would read as one group of three ratings; they are not in a row.
infoIcon.scaffoldingNote: The info icons are parented to the Insight band frame, not to the Card, because a Card instance cannot host children. They are absolutely positioned over each card. The ICON ITSELF is a published library instance — only its parentage is scaffolded.

tooltips.component: Tooltip 167:15, key fed5b8b3a7e259df7bf4fcff6f2a9849d54ec4fd. A plain COMPONENT with one property, Label#167:9.
tooltips.componentWasCorrect: Tooltip, not Popover. Every reasoning string is read-only prose. Each was checked for whether it implies an action; none does. The actions those events imply (Review, Accept, Reply) already exist as the Action column on the ledger rows themselves, so the reasoning never needs to carry one. The brief asked to stop and report if any reasoning needed an action — none did.

howTheTwoKindsWereDistinguished.method: Not by inventing a second component or a new style. By content shape, using the substrate MUI already specifies.
howTheTwoKindsWereDistinguished.controlLabel: Thumb tooltips name a control: "Helpful" and "Not useful". One line, the component hugs its text, 70x24.
howTheTwoKindsWereDistinguished.reasoning: Info tooltips carry the reasoning. The Label is set long, the text node is switched to textAutoResize HEIGHT and set to FILL, and the root is fixed at 300 — which is MUI Tooltip maxWidth, documented in the component own description. They render 300x72 to 300x120, three to seven lines.
howTheTwoKindsWereDistinguished.ratio: A reasoning tooltip is roughly 4x to 5x the area of a control label at the same 11px type. The difference is unmissable at rest and does not depend on any styling the library has not settled.
howTheTwoKindsWereDistinguished.whyThisIsTranscriptionNotInvention: The Tooltip description carries a PENDING DESIGNER CLARIFICATION that explicitly warns against guessing at "a size/multiline treatment". Wrapping at 300 is NOT a guess — maxWidth 300 is recorded in that same description as MUI substrate. No new surface, radius, colour, arrow or placement chrome was introduced. If the designer later specifies a distinct reasoning treatment, this changes.

reasoningText.rule: Every event named is a row in the ledger on the same screen. Nothing was invented.
reasoningText.deliberateOmission: The card 1 synthesis statement says "up from 8.1% in March". March appears nowhere in the ledger, so the reasoning does not cite it. The reasoning names only what the reader can verify by looking down the page.
reasoningText.card1: Built from two ledger events: the 18 Jul office visit — diabetes follow-up, Dr. Reyes — and the 21 Aug lab, Hemoglobin A1C 9.4%, above the 7.0% goal. No therapy change is recorded between them: the only medication entries are a 28 Jul nurse triage call on metformin tolerance and a 14 Aug metformin 1000 mg ER refill at the same dose.
reasoningText.card2: An outgoing ophthalmology referral for diabetic retinopathy screening was sent 5 Aug. No appointment has been recorded against it in the 24 days since. On 29 Aug the patient messaged reporting four days of blurred vision.
reasoningText.card3: An incoming referral from Dr. Alvarez, endocrinology, arrived 18 Aug and is still marked awaiting acceptance. No response has been recorded against it in the 13 days since, and the ledger holds no scheduled future visit.
reasoningText.whyNotARestatement: The brief was explicit that "why am I seeing this" means naming the events, not rephrasing the headline. Each string names dated ledger rows and, where the insight rests on an absence, names the absence and the window it covers.
